I

The path

From a night in Tehran to a desk in Berlin.

IThe path

8 and 9 January 2026

Tehran, Haft Hoz

Protests had spread across the country for twelve days.

On the evening of the 8th the blackout began. The internet went dark across the country, all at once.

For two nights, security forces fired into the streets.

I was there.

The drawing is real. The man carrying the wounded girl is me. The girl with the flag is holding me up with her other hand, so I don’t fall and can get her to safety. The banner is the one thing I added. I may still have it tattooed.

IThe path

A blackout is information architecture used as a weapon.

3,117

killed, by the state’s own count

6,126

killed and verified by rights monitors, with 17,091 more deaths under investigation

5,000–20,000

the range given by the UN Special Rapporteur

400+ hours

without a working internet

Uncounted

The dead could not be counted.

Unfound

The wounded could not be found.

Sealed

Each family’s grief was sealed off from every other.

Late January 2026. State TV; HRANA; UN Special Rapporteur Mai Sato; NetBlocks. The gap between the counts is the blackout’s work.
IThe path

Every day after, it got worse.

Ninety days, drawn to scale. The bars grow as the country closed in.

Just as everything was falling apart, I came to Berlin.

The Wall, 1961–1989

A city that once fell apart and found itself again.

IThe path

A name I heard by chance.

One night, by chance, a historian mentioned a Persian paper once printed in Berlin. Its name was Kāveh.

1916–1922, Berlin-Charlottenburg

Founded by Hasan Taqizadeh and written by Iranians in the city, in Persian, for readers far away.

Its emblem

The Derafsh-e Kaviani: Kaveh raising the banner, the people behind him.

Two lives

First a wartime paper, paid for by Germany. From 1920, a journal of literature and history.

What it meant to me

A century earlier, from this city, someone had tried to give Iranians a public language. Kavian is not its continuation. It is a rhyme, in a city where I can speak, study and build in the open.

Sources: “Kāveh (majalleh),” Persian Wikipedia; Iraj Afshar, “Kāva newspaper,” Encyclopaedia Iranica. Image: Wikimedia Commons.
IThe path

Berlin: wonder, between chaos and order.

Chaos

At home, a war. Every morning the news from the country I had left was worse than the night before.

Order

Here, a city that runs on time. Forms, a room, a desk. From 12 March, a university.

Wonder

Bronzes of people carrying people, in the parks. A Persian paper from 1916 called Kāveh. The freedom to say all of this out loud.

A new path: studying data science and building with AI, with the same question underneath it.

IThe path

In Berlin, it all meets.

All of this is what made me think of Kavian.

II

Kavian

A dossier people can read.

IIKavian

Kavian helps people, first in Iran, understand a collective problem, see how power acted, weigh what each option costs and decide for themselves.

Not a verdict
Not the voice of “the people”
Not yet a running system
درفش کاویانی

Kaveh raises his apron against Zahhak, a darkness that feeds on people’s lives. Then he returns to his own life. He does not take the throne.

The banner was later jeweled into a royal standard. If advisers, a model or the founder take the choice, it is a flag of power again.

III

Architecture

From far away, then closer. A design, not yet a running system.

IIIArchitecture

Seen from far away.

Something happensA decision, a promise, a price, a crackdown
→
KavianGathers, checks, compares, explains
→
A person understandsand chooses for themselves

Kavian stands between an event and a person’s decision. It never makes the decision.

IIIArchitecture

Every system decides what counts before anyone looks.

Before

Many people judge, each time, where everyone can see.

After

One person decides once, upstream. A machine repeats that decision thousands of times, out of sight.

I learned this building a risk model: the answer to “what counts as a delay?” was mine, set once. Kavian keeps that kind of choice visible, and open to challenge.

IIIArchitecture

Five jobs around one dossier.

Collect

Bring in news, documents, data and people’s own accounts.

Check

Ask what supports each claim, and what is missing.

Discuss

Send each piece to people who can see it differently.

Show

Give the public a clear view of what is known and disputed.

Remember

Keep every version, so no correction erases the past.

IIIArchitecture

People judge. Machines do the paperwork.

People

Raise a problem

Tell what they lived

Review and disagree

Decide what is published

Choose what to do

judgment

Machines

Read and sort material

Draft a first summary

Translate, Persian first

Notice where accounts conflict

Keep the record of every change

IIIArchitecture

Follow one question.

An invented example, to show the moving parts. Not a real city, not a finding.

1A fare goes up

The transit authority says it keeps routes running.

2Material arrives

A budget table, a timetable, riders saying their buses thinned.

3The question is split

What the records say. What is likely next year. Whether it is fair.

4Reviewers look

A budget reader, a transport expert, a language reader. A rider adds what is missing.

5Views side by side

They agree on the numbers. They differ on whether a longer walk is a fair price.

6A person reads

What is sourced, what is estimated, what is a value dispute, how to correct it.

IIIArchitecture

The whole loop.

The same journey, drawn as one loop. It never closes: new evidence opens it again.

The jointPeople actA machine assists

Like the banner’s four arms around one centre: one subject, four kinds of question, each answered a different way.

find, extract, compare

organize the range

Is a longer walk a fair price?
The people who live with it. Experts only clarify
none

IIIArchitecture

Five machine helpers, each with a limit.

In software these are called agents. Here they are clerks: one job each, and a red line they do not cross.

Stops here
Scribe

Takes material in, notes where it came from, drafts a first card

Does not decide a claim is true

Router

Sends each card to the right kind of review

Does not choose the public’s preference

Mirror

Sets feedback side by side: support, contest, unknown

Does not average positions into one voice

Interpreter

Plain language, Persian first, then other languages

Does not replace the original card

Keeper

Keeps every version and receipt; blacks out private details

Does not publish private detail in the name of transparency

IIIArchitecture

These models sort. A person chooses.

A few small models answer only a fixed question, and they say how sure they are. Jev does this as a hosted service. Laya does it with open weights. Neither writes, argues, or decides.

Which one?

Picks one answer from a fixed listWhich kind of question is this: fact, estimate, value, action, mixed?

How likely?

Says how likely a yes isWould publishing this text as written expose someone?

How much?

Places something on a scaleHow far does the text make its claim inspectable?

The ability is the slot, not one vendor. Persian civic text is untested. Thresholds are precautions, not tuned on Kavian’s data. Never on the value row.

The conductor

Moves each piece of work from helper to helper, and pauses where a person must approve.

LangGraph, LangChain

The models

Language models draft and translate. A decision model only sorts a fixed question and reports how sure it is.

Each model is a slot. No single vendor decides.

Records every input, step, model call and human edit.

Where it lives

Runs online. Every change to the code is versioned.

Vercel, GitHub
hosted

The history of the system itself can be inspected.

Components as designed; configuration not yet audited. Open tools help inspection, but independence is shown in rules, data and a way to contest the people who run it.
IIIArchitecture

How it could fail, and the guard.

A familiar circle becomes a quiet veto

Reviewers are chosen by the question, with conflicts disclosed

A confident machine is read as the truth

Machines give labels, never findings; a person confirms

The record exposes the people it protects

Layered views and redaction before publication

“Open source” is offered as proof of independence

Replaceable parts, and operators who can be challenged

A smooth summary erases a real disagreement

Positions stay side by side, each with its reason

Attention is counted as success

Count understanding, corrections and harm reduced

IVThe proposal

Where I want to go.

Now

A design, and a question I cannot put down.

The year at the centre

Seminars, the Lab, consultancy. An essay, a charter, a gate tested on Persian text.

After

A first living dossier, in public, that people in Iran can read, question and correct.

A life

An ordinary life in Berlin: to study, work and rest, without the ground moving under me every week.

A work

Time and depth for Kavian, among people who can tell me where it is wrong.

The programme’s support, and its rhythm of seminars and consultancy, would give me both.

IVThe proposal

I bring

Years of building production AI and systems, a question lived at close range, and a Persian-first view.

I ask

The seminars, the Intelligence Design Lab, the final-project consultancy, and the critique of faculty and peers.

It returns

A public essay, a Kavian charter, and a question-type gate tested on Persian text.

The banner exists so that life returns to people.
